Class GrovePicoShield

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.grove.GrovePicoShield
public final class GrovePicoShield extends Object
Pin map for Seeed's passive Grove Shield for Pi Pico v1.0 on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. The shield adds no protocol or runtime object: every socket is an ordinary Pico pin, so these resolved pins can be passed directly to a Grove driver or to Gpio. Each getter returns the socket's primary SIG pin.

The digital sockets carry the GPIO number in their silkscreen label (D16 is GP16), and the analog sockets A0..A2 are the Pico's ADC pins GP26..GP28, read with Gpio.analogRead. Plug I2C modules, such as the Grove OLED display, into the I2C0 socket and pass getI2c0(), the bus on its GP8/GP9, to their driver. The I2C1 socket pins are exposed for drivers that wire their own bus. UART0, UART1 and SPI0 expose their signal pins individually, so a serial or SPI driver can select the socket without duplicating the shield's pinout.

The shield seen from above, USB at the top, each socket's pins as printed under it. The first pin is the SIG wire its getter returns. The analog sockets always take 3.3 V; the others take VCC from the power switch. 

+----------------------------[ USB ]-----------------------------+
| SPI0  GND o o SCK                              VCC switch:  5V |
|       3V3 o o TX                                           3V3 |
|       CS  o o RX                                               |
|                                                                |
| UART0  RX=GP1 TX=GP0                    I2C0  SCL=GP9  SDA=GP8 |
| [RX |TX |VCC|GND]                            [SCL|SDA|VCC|GND] |
| UART1  RX=GP5 TX=GP4                    I2C1  SCL=GP7  SDA=GP6 |
| [RX |TX |VCC|GND]        Raspberry Pi        [SCL|SDA|VCC|GND] |
| D16  SIG=GP16              Pico 2 W               A0  SIG=GP26 |
| [D16|D17|VCC|GND]        (sits here)         [A0 |NC |3V3|GND] |
| D18  SIG=GP18                                     A1  SIG=GP27 |
| [D18|D19|VCC|GND]                            [A1 |A0 |3V3|GND] |
| D20  SIG=GP20                                     A2  SIG=GP28 |
| [D20|D21|VCC|GND]                            [A2 |A1 |3V3|GND] |
+-------------------[ DEBUG: SWCLK GND SWDIO ]-------------------+

  Socket  Getter                            Pico pin
  D16     getD16()                          GP16
  D18     getD18()                          GP18
  D20     getD20()                          GP20
  A0      getA0()                           GP26 (ADC0)
  A1      getA1()                           GP27 (ADC1)
  A2      getA2()                           GP28 (ADC2)
  I2C0    getI2c0() bus, getI2c0Sda/Scl()   GP8, GP9
  I2C1    getI2c1Sda(), getI2c1Scl()        GP6, GP7
  UART0    getUart0Rx()/getUart0Tx()        GP1, GP0
  UART1    getUart1Rx()/getUart1Tx()        GP5, GP4
  SPI0     getSpi0Miso()/getSpi0Mosi()      GP16, GP19
           getSpi0Sck()/getSpi0Cs()        GP18, GP17

      public I2c getI2c0()
      The I2C bus behind the I2C0 socket (SDA GP8, SCL GP9), to pass to a Grove I2C driver such as GroveOledSsd1315. It is the Pico's Wire bus, the same instance RaspberryPico2.getI2c() returns, on every call.
